Raṅganātha
------------------------------------------
Raṅganātha, along with वरदराज of काञ्चीपुरम् and वेङ्कटेश of तिरुपति, is the most popular aspect of विष्णु worshipped in South India. The well-known temple at श्रीरङ्गम् in Tamil Nadu is the very heart of the श्रीवैष्णव cult. This temple—at least the original icon—is said to have been born out of the ocean and given by Śrī राम to विभीषण. While carrying it from अयोध्या to लङ्का, विभीषण placed it on the ground at the present site, in order to rest a while. Unfortunately for him (and fortunately for others!) it got firmly fixed there!
The image is of the Yogaśayana type (lying on the serpent-bed in योग) with only two hands, the right hand apparently supporting the head while the left rests on the serpent-bed.
The lotus with ब्रह्मा, the आयुध-puruṣas (the weapons in human form), the demons मधु and कैटभ who were killed by him, as also some sages like भृगु and मार्कण्डेय are often depicted along with the Lord.
Similar Yogaśayana images are found in Śrīraṅgapaṭna of Karnataka and Tiruvanantapuram of Kerala where it is known as Padmanābha or Anantaśayana.
